nom: La Roche-Posay Effaclar Acne Face Wash with 4% Benzoyl Peroxide

segments.sensitive: Sensitive-skin reviewers are split: many say it's gentle enough for daily use with no burning or irritation, including some specifically calling it sensitive-skin approved, while several others report burning, rash, itchiness, or irritation, particularly around the nose, with a few advising starting slowly or consulting a dermatologist first.
segments.oily: Reviewers with oily or combination-oily skin recommend it for controlling breakouts, saying it removes excess oil without leaving skin dry or tight.
segments.combination: One reviewer with combination-oily, sensitive skin found the cream cleanser didn't penetrate daily oil and grime well enough and saw no change over three to four months; another with combination skin says it cured her forehead acne after months of a different regimen.
segments.dry: One reviewer with mostly dry skin found it felt smooth and calls it effective and gentle; another with dry, sensitive skin reported no issues despite her skin type.

concerns.dehydration: Many reviewers say it cleans without leaving skin dry, tight, or stripped even with daily use; a substantial number of others, especially with frequent use, describe it as drying and recommend following with a moisturizer or limiting use to every other day.
concerns.redness: Several reviewers, including some managing rosacea, say the cleanser reduces redness and calms active breakouts without irritation; one reviewer experienced slight redness when she first started, which resolved as her skin adapted.
concerns.barrier: A couple of reviewers say the formula's strength doesn't compromise the skin barrier and is gentler on it than stronger benzoyl peroxide products they've tried.
concerns.blemishes: The large majority of reviewers with acne-prone skin, including some managing hormonal, cystic, or stress-related acne, report noticeably fewer breakouts and faster clearing of active blemishes within days to a few weeks of consistent use; a couple of reviewers saw no improvement even after three to four months.
concerns.oiliness: Reviewers with oily or combination skin say it removes excess oil and leftover makeup without leaving skin feeling stripped or overly dry.

aspects.libelle: Possible temporary purging period before results

extraits.texte: Although it says it is good for sensitive skin, I would disagree. I used this three nights in a row and here I am with a rash and itchiness on my face and neck. Same thing happened to me with the Murad AHA/BHA exfoliating cleanser, atleast this one wasn't as pricey.

I really wanted this cleanser to work. It was my understanding that this cleanser was a "replacement" for the Step-3 Duo Dual Action Acne Treatment cream for the Effaclar line. I really do wish that La Roche Posay would reformulate that cream. The original 3 step system was perfect for my skin and now I'm back to breaking out at 34 yrs old, like I did when I was 15 and stressing about it isn't helping. I've never done well with cream cleansers as a combo-oily, sensitive skin user. I don't feel that they penetrate well enough through daily oil and grime, even after doing an oil/makeup removing cleanser. With that said, only using the SA Cleanser and Toner with the retinoid gel as a substitute step 3 isn't cutting it - I also add in Niacinamide, Hyaluronic Acid and Retinol serums into that regimen. However, in an effort to use up the bottle (since this is a higher cost brand), I've been using the cream cleanser in the mornings and the gel cleanser in the evenings. I haven't seen a change in the last 3-4 months since I bought it. LRP has been really good to my skin in the last 5-6 years, and I really hope they are working to reformulate the BP cream to move back to the original 3-step system for the Effaclar line. I really don't want to have to do research for another skin care brand and go through the whole process again of seeing if it works.

Since I started using this cleanser, I've noticed a significant improvement in the appearance of my skin. At first, I was a bit skeptical about using a product with benzoyl peroxide because I had read that it could be irritating. However, I was pleasantly surprised by how gentle it is. The texture is lightweight and feels refreshing upon application. After a few weeks of use, my acne breakouts have noticeably decreased, and my skin feels clearer and more balanced. I use it every morning and night, and although I experienced slight redness at first, my skin has adapted well. It's important not to overdo it with the amount since a little goes a long way. Additionally, I appreciate that it is fragrance-free, which is a big plus for my sensitive skin. However, I give it a 4 instead of a 5 because I feel it could be a bit more hydrating, especially during the colder months. Overall, I am very satisfied with the results and would definitely recommend it to those struggling with acne.

I RARELY recommend or review products but this… I seriously LOVE this and it has worked so well for my skin!! I have oily, acne prone skin with occasional cystic acne. I had a cystic pimple pop up and ran out lf the cleanserbi was useing and decided to try this. Im so glad I did bc this is my new favorite!! Only been 4 days and I am already seeing results🙌
Great for my acne rosacea. removes dirt and grime without irritation. Grateful for this cleanser as its effective as panoxyl but more gentler on my skin and moister barrier.

This face wash felt very smooth on my skin and I suffer from mostly dry skin. As someone that grew up using benzoyl peroxide to treat my acne, this is such a game changer! It doesn't have a strong scent as long as you use the recommended amount. I would defiantly recommend this.

I needed something new for my skin care routine and I got this to try for free and it has been a game changer. Personally I have to use about every other day because it does dry my skin out but I am also super sensitive. But every other day has cleared my small acne patches
